subject: Inference spend fit — post-call follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Sharma <r.sharma@bluewave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inference spend fit — post-call follow-up & next steps

Hi Rajiv — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our 45-minute discovery so we have shared alignment and clear next steps.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- Query volume spike during settlement windows causes variable latency and surprises on spend.
- Current provider charges per-request with poor batching; engineering can't rely on guarantees for peak throughput.
- Procurement has a strict upper bound for initial pilot spend (~$12k/mo) to get exec approval.

Goals we heard:
1) Validate production throughput at 200–300 QPS sustained for core inference path (short sequences).
2) Reduce per-authorization cost by ~30% vs your current vendor through batching, prefix caching, and a model-size/quantization tradeoff.
3) Pilot in non-PII scope for 6 weeks, with clear metrics to take to procurement (latency p50/p95, tokens / request, and monthly bill projection).

Preliminary economics (back-of-envelope from today's call):
- Baseline tokens per auth: ~420 tokens (prompt + response).
- Without batching: estimated ~1.5M tokens/day => ~45M tokens/month.
- Options to hit budget (~$12k/mo):
  * Aggressive batching (continuous batching window 25–50 ms) + KV prefix cache: ~35–45% reduction in tokens billed per logical request.
  * Medium quantization model variant (8-bit, Redwood-verified): additional ~20–25% token-cost-equivalent saving via cheaper instance types.
  * Hybrid routing: keep small fraction of traffic on low-latency tier and rest on cost-optimized instances.

What I need from you to firm numbers:
- A 48–72h sample of anonymized scoring logs (timestamps, input token counts, average response length). The CSV schema I attached should be enough (bluewave_scoring_sample.csv).
- Confirmation you can run pilot in a non-PII environment or provide a short list of approved fields to hash.

Proposed next steps / mutual action plan:
1) You send anonymized sample logs by EOD Thu (Oct 22).
2) Redwood run a 5-day pilot sim locally to generate batching/cost scenarios and a 30-day bill projection (deliverable: Pilot Economics Brief).
3) Align on pilot scope + SOW draft for procurement — target delivery Tue Oct 27.
4) Procurement check-in and decision window the week of Nov 2.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-scope.pdf (pilot template), bluewave_scoring_sample.csv (CSV schema).

If this matches your recollection, I’ll lock in those dates and start the sim as soon as we have the logs.

Thanks,
Mina

—
Mina Haddad
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-18T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inference spend fit — post-call follow-up & next steps

Mina — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers:

- We can provide the anonymized scoring logs, goal is to sanitize account ids and any card-adjacent fields. Will share CSV by Fri Oct 23 EOD (legal asked for one extra day).
- Pilot scope: we can run it in our staging environment (no PII) — procurement only needs a short note that traffic is synthetic/staging.
- The $12k/month cap is firm for the initial pilot; we’ll need the 30-day bill projection to show cost delta vs our current vendor.

Two asks for Redwood team:
1) In the Pilot Economics Brief, please include both token-based projection and an instance-hour projection so our finance folks can compare apples-to-apples.
2) Give a short tradeoff table: latency impact vs cost savings for each knob (batching window, prefix cache hit rates, quantization level).

If you can hit those asks, procurement and I should be able to get the SOW moving.

Thanks — Rajiv
Rajiv Sharma
Head of Risk & Authorizations, BlueWave Payments
r.sharma@bluewave.com | +1 213-555-0820

Rajiv — thanks for the quick turn. Confirming we’ll incorporate your asks into the deliverable. A few clarifications so expectations are aligned:

- Deliverables for the pilot economics brief (target: Oct 27):
  * Token projection (30-day) with low/medium/high scenarios tied to batching latency (25ms / 50ms / 100ms windows).
  * Instance-hour estimate per model variant and quantization level (float16 / 8-bit / 4-bit where applicable).
  * Tradeoff table: expected p50/p95 latency change vs percent cost delta for each knob.
  * Short ops checklist for integration: KV cache TTL suggestions, prefix keying guidance, and a 2-step fall-back routing plan.

- Timeline update: we can start sims as soon as we get the sample logs; if logs arrive Fri Oct 23 we’ll deliver the brief Tue Oct 27. If procurement needs the SOW earlier, we can draft a concise SOW placeholder with the pilot budget range.

I’ve attached the CSV schema again and a short pilot template. Ben will run the sim and Marissa will own the economics brief.

Next check-in: how does Thu Oct 22 at 10am PT for a 30-minute alignment call sound (we can invite procurement)?

Thanks,
Mina
